summary.whatChanges: Zod's base64 and base64url string formats now carry a lax charset regex as their runtime `pattern` (actual validity still enforced by the isValidBase64 helpers), while JSON Schema generation swaps that lax regex back to the exact block-structure regex for both `pattern` and record `patternProperties`.
behaviorChanges: z.templateLiteral([...,z.base64()]) now composes correctly: prefixed values like "id-AAAA" validate and bare "AAAA" is rejected, where the old ^$| alternation leaked
Parsing multi-megabyte base64/base64url values inside template literals no longer overflows the regex stack
z.toJSONSchema() on base64/base64url still emits the exact quantified pattern despite the laxer runtime regex
looseRecord with a base64url key now emits regexes.base64url.source in patternProperties instead of the charset-only regex
schema._zod.def.pattern for base64 is now the charset regex /^[0-9a-zA-Z+/]*={0,2}$/ rather than regexes.base64
risks: Code reading schema._zod.def.pattern directly (custom codegen, other JSON Schema emitters) now gets a permissive regex that accepts invalid base64 such as "A" or "AAAAA"
The lax-to-exact swap is keyed by RegExp identity in a Map; any path that clones or recreates the pattern object loses the swap and emits the lax pattern
Template literals composing base64 accept the lax block-less charset, so a base64 segment of invalid length may pass inside a template literal even though z.base64() alone rejects it
base64urlCharset/base64Charset are now exported from core schemas, widening the public surface
